verdict.rationale: Homebrew is a package manager that could plausibly ship background automation (e.g., scheduled updates), so the axis applies. The evidence shows only non-interactive building blocks: NONINTERACTIVE installs, MDM workflows, and an as-console-user command meant to be invoked from external scheduled jobs. The scheduling itself relies on host-platform tooling, and no Homebrew-native capability to set up autonomous background automations is documented. The 'start any services' mention concerns running installed software, which is an adjacent feature, not user-defined automations.
